awd_titl_txt: Scaling Nationwide Identification and Support of Extraordinary Young Mathematicians
awd_abstract_narration:
The United States has no national system for identifying and developing its most mathematically talented K-12 students. Research indicates that early mathematical ability strongly predicts later scientific and economic contributions, yet many of the nation's most promising young mathematicians go unrecognized, particularly in rural and lower-income communities where systematic screening is rare. This project will expand National Math Stars, a nonprofit initiative that combines universal, data-driven screening of elementary school students with a decade of academic, mentoring, and financial support for those identified as having profound mathematical ability. By reaching a larger share of the eligible student population and testing new approaches to sustaining engagement and reducing the cost of support, the project will strengthen the nation's long-term scientific and economic competitiveness, while helping ensure that talented children can develop their abilities regardless of where they live or their family's income.

The project consists of two interconnected workstreams. First, National Math Stars will scale its existing talent identification and support model from ten states to a projected 75 percent of the U.S. population by 2030, partnering with state education agencies and school districts to screen more than 1.8 million students annually and enroll over 4,100 students in decade-long support tracks. The project will monitor reach, retention, cost-effectiveness, and mathematical growth using nationally normed assessments, comparing new cohorts against earlier program years to assess whether impact is sustained at scale. Second, the project will design, build, and iteratively test an SI-assisted digital platform intended to extend personalized academic guidance to a larger population of students at lower cost per-student than current staff-intensive advising.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.
